topic: Numerical evidence for seven European safeguard routes; inputs, not estimated coordinates

facts.claim: Lot 1 Phase 1 requires at least 25,000 H100-equivalent accelerators per project.
facts.coordinateUse: Scale of a single-facility conditional route; not a protected numerator.
facts.limits: No installed capacity or public-access hours established; no maximum deployment size.

facts.claim: Lot 2 Phase 1 requires at least 40,000 H100-equivalent accelerators per project.
facts.coordinateUse: Alternative single-project scale.
facts.limits: A one-project protocol cannot inherit all seven projects' capacity.

facts.claim: Four Lot 1 projects and three Lot 2 projects imply 4*25,000+3*40,000=220,000 minimum planned equivalents.
facts.coordinateUse: Conditional whole-programme design scope only.
facts.limits: Seven projects need not mean seven physical sites; multisite projects allowed. Not an upper bound on actual built capacity, nor an estimate of protected compute.

facts.claim: Up to EUR 1 billion is available under the current MFF for Phase 1; national contributions must at least match EU contributions.
facts.coordinateUse: Financing scale and dependency; not affected coverage or spending.
facts.limits: Per-project EU funding additionally capped at 17% IT CAPEX. Future EUR 4bn is conditional post-2027, not available Geneva funding.

facts.claim: Set-up may run for up to 18 months after FWC and first specific-contract signature; operational readiness requires a technical audit.
facts.coordinateUse: Disallows assuming live hardware validation by June 2027 from tender dates alone.
facts.limits: Not expected duration, not a minimum, and signature date unknown; tabletop protocol testing is a smaller endpoint.

facts.claim: Phase 1 service payments start at operational readiness and continue for five years.
facts.coordinateUse: Potential persistence of a future agreed protocol.
facts.limits: Not five years of guaranteed safeguarded activity as of cutoff.

facts.claim: The notified party has 15 days from receipt to submit observations before the terminating party's final decision.
facts.coordinateUse: Concrete remedy latency component.
facts.limits: Not incident notification SLA, total remediation duration, or automatic shutdown.

facts.claim: I.14.6 requires notification without delay, continued information and mitigation; it does not quantify notification in hours.
facts.locator: p.20 I.14.6; p.21 I.15.2 end-user terms
facts.coordinateUse: Existing procedural foundation requiring an operational definition.
facts.limits: Model-originated harm scope and tenant evidence rights unresolved.

facts.claim: A formal national contracting-authority commitment letter is mandatory for a proposed host state; consortium members supply a coordinator mandate and declarations.
facts.coordinateUse: Evidence of indispensable financing and representation gates.
facts.limits: Does not identify the selected project, number of states or all underlying appropriation approvals.

facts.claim: End users must sign terms with the contractor before access; contractor may suspend or restrict activity posing infrastructure, security or compliance risks and must notify contracting authorities without undue delay.
facts.locator: p.21 I.15.2–3; p.20 I.14.7 additional security measures
facts.coordinateUse: Existing implementation and remedy path for a negotiated incident protocol.
facts.limits: Does not establish that all model-originated harm triggers suspension, that an external evaluator has access rights, or that proposed terms are adopted.

facts.claim: If consensus fails, Public Governance Body decisions require at least 75% of all voting rights including absent members; the Commission has an indivisible 50%, and national authorities share 50% in proportion to committed specific-contract contributions.
facts.unit: fraction of all voting rights required
facts.locator: pp.21–22 I.16.2; prior approval matters in I.16.5
facts.coordinateUse: Concrete voting arithmetic for matters within this body's remit, rather than invented equal-party consent counts.
facts.limits: Not a universal threshold for changing the FWC or imposing a model-safety protocol; selected national members and weights unknown, and contractor has observer status without a vote.

gaps.reason: Draft design and historical EuroHPC annual report do not establish a 2026 AIGF award, signature or purchased hours. Tender windows extend beyond cutoff.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Award notice, executed FWC/SC1 and unit-price/volume schedule for the chosen project.

gaps.reason: Live procurement page produced no readable body in this pass. Earlier repo evidence reports Oct 26 extension to Feb 4 2027 for Lot 1 and Dec 3 2026 for Lot 2; not independently refreshed here.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Reopen current portal announcements and correcting TED notice; do not extend the old question deadline by inference.

gaps.reason: Notification/remedy and national commitment gates are documented, but no selected contractor, agreed model-incident taxonomy or tenant flow-down.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Authoritative clarification and signed user terms with the selected contractor; measure a protocol drill separately from operational capacity.

coordinateReadiness.x: Partial: draft procedure and maximum set-up duration are quantified; approval and actual execution dates remain unknown.
coordinateReadiness.y: Design envelope and one-project minimum scales available. No measured affected accelerator-hours or safety effectiveness; no scalar coordinate justified.

facts.claim: Belgium receives 7.4% of total LUMI computing time under the stated allocation scheme.
facts.locator: Getting compute time on LUMI, first paragraph
facts.coordinateUse: Whole-channel conditional envelope.
facts.limits: Not actual AI use or pilot coverage; already inside national 50%.

facts.claim: Preparatory/development applications may request at most 25,000 GPU-hours.
facts.period: 2025 instructions still linked by current access page
facts.locator: Instructions, paragraph beginning LUMI-BE Preparatory; billing section
facts.coordinateUse: Realistic single-award upper bound, conditional on eligibility and award; pilot safeguarded amount currently unmeasured.
facts.limits: Code development/benchmarking only, not production model training; any CPU request reduces GPU allowance proportionately.

facts.claim: Regular projects may request at most 500,000 GPU-hours and run one year.
facts.coordinateUse: Alternative production-award ceiling, not total Belgian allocation.
facts.limits: Not an awarded amount; all listed 2026 regular deadlines were past at cutoff.

facts.claim: Panel aims to notify applicants one month after the deadline; preparatory applications are reviewed monthly.
facts.locator: Instructions paragraph beginning Applications will be evaluated; access-page preparatory paragraph
facts.coordinateUse: Observed administrative design supports a small pre-Geneva application path.
facts.limits: Not observed turnaround distribution or time to negotiate new safety terms.

facts.claim: Preparatory benchmarking normally lasts four months, extendable at application to up to one year with justification.
facts.locator: Instructions, purposes 2 and 3; no extensions after granting
facts.coordinateUse: Bounded project design fits within the 233-day cutoff-to-Geneva interval if promptly approved.
facts.limits: Fit is calendar feasibility only; software work and new terms not pre-approved.

facts.claim: One full LUMI-G node-hour costs four Belgian GPU-hours; each MI250X package presents two GPU compute dies to software.
facts.locator: About CPU, GPU and storage billing; paragraph beginning On LUMI-G
facts.coordinateUse: 25,000 package-hours correspond to 6,250 full node-hours under this definition.
facts.limits: EuroHPC annual-report strategic table instead displays about eight GPU-hours/node-hour; do not pool unharmonised GPU figures.

facts.claim: The required acknowledgement names BELSPO, SPW, Flemish EWI and Innoviris as four LUMI-BE partners.
facts.coordinateUse: Identifies additional authority-retrieval targets beyond VSC and CECI.
facts.limits: Not proof that all four must sign each pilot or policy amendment; EuroCC funders page describes a different programme.

facts.claim: Instructions already request AI methods including generative language modelling and virtual agents, and actual compute/storage plans.
facts.locator: AI methods list and Detailed questions 3–4
facts.coordinateUse: Do not claim an AI-use declaration is wholly new; version-bound evaluation and incident evidence would be additions.
facts.limits: No model-safety pass/fail gate shown.

facts.claim: LUMI gives at least two weeks' notice before amended terms take effect; continued use is deemed acceptance.
facts.coordinateUse: One implementation latency component.
facts.limits: Not blanket authority for Belgian allocators to rewrite host terms or obtain external evaluation rights.

gaps.reason: Quota, application ceilings and system-wide utilisation found; no deduplicated Belgian award/usage-by-AI-method ledger retrieved.
gaps.nextRetrieval: LUMI-BE annual allocation return and project-level actual usage matched to existing AI-method fields.

gaps.reason: Operational allocators, funding partners and host terms identified, not the legal delegation for this appendix.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Belgian joint programme agreement and delegation; CSC-approved appendix plus one eligible recipient's acceptance.

gaps.reason: Current page lists only past 2026 regular dates. Monthly preparatory route exists but is narrower.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Updated Belgian 2027 call; use preparatory ceilings only for eligible development/benchmark work.

coordinateReadiness.x: Partial: monthly review, one-month decision target, four-month benchmark duration, two-week service-terms notice. No probability or exact consent count.
coordinateReadiness.y: 7.4% channel envelope plus 25,000/500,000 package-GPU-hour per-project ceilings. Missing actual AI awards and adopted-safeguard numerator.

facts.claim: EuroHPC allocates half of LUMI resources.
facts.coordinateUse: Conditional whole-channel envelope.
facts.limits: Not half of all AI workloads or current safeguarded compute.

facts.claim: 2025 AI-for-science/collaborative EU calls awarded LUMI-G 1,024,836 node-hours.
facts.locator: p.57 Table 15 LUMI-G column; p.58 Table 16
facts.coordinateUse: Historical AI-specific route exposure, not merely a generic compute budget.
facts.limits: Awards, not consumption; includes prior AI/data-intensive call cutoffs; not bound by proposed protocol.

facts.claim: Industrial AI calls awarded LUMI-G 251,875 node-hours: 10,625 playground, 78,750 fast lane and 162,500 large scale.
facts.coordinateUse: AI-specific historical capacity and three practical access paths.
facts.limits: Not an industrial recipient count or actual usage; no current safety-appendix adoption.

facts.claim: Regular Access awarded LUMI-G 876,816 node-hours.
facts.coordinateUse: Additional channel exposure; AI share unknown.
facts.limits: Not all regular projects are AI; do not classify as AI-specific.

facts.claim: Extreme Scale Access awarded LUMI-G 3,292,485 node-hours.
facts.coordinateUse: Large-allocation exposure; scope a prospective tranche condition against actual award.
facts.limits: Not measured AI volume.

facts.claim: Six listed competitive LUMI-G access categories total 5,917,012 node-hours: 120,000 benchmark +351,000 development +1,024,836 AI science +251,875 industrial AI +876,816 regular +3,292,485 extreme.
facts.locator: pp.57–59 Table 16; constituent sums in claim
facts.coordinateUse: Matched historical denominator for a specifically restricted call-population comparison.
facts.limits: Excludes strategic allocations and national pool; not total installed capacity or all awards.

facts.claim: AI-labelled calls account for (1,024,836+251,875)/5,917,012 = 0.2157695472 of listed competitive LUMI-G node-hours.
facts.coordinateUse: Lower bound on explicitly AI-classified categories in this denominator; prioritisation input.
facts.limits: Other modes may contain AI. This is not a safety coverage fraction or current AI share.

facts.claim: Strategic access separately lists LUMI-G 1,236,723 node-hours and 9,893,780 GPU-hours.
facts.coordinateUse: Makes the competitive-denominator exclusion explicit.
facts.limits: GPU/node ratio about eight differs from Belgian package accounting; preserve native node-hours.

facts.claim: Benchmark/development evaluation is designed to allocate resources within at most two weeks after monthly cutoff.
facts.coordinateUse: Pre-Geneva administrative timing input for small pilot.
facts.limits: Not actual SLA attainment or safeguard negotiation duration.

facts.claim: Regular Access evaluation runs over four months; Executive Director submits ranked results to Governing Board for final approval.
facts.coordinateUse: Complete award-review chain clearer than earlier notes; distinct from terms-amendment authority.
facts.limits: No vote/consent denominator for a new model-evaluation condition.

facts.claim: AI-for-science evaluation has maximum one month duration with six cutoffs per year.
facts.coordinateUse: More route-relevant timeline than general regular access.
facts.limits: Scientific/technical/ethical review is not adoption of this evidence-access protocol.

facts.claim: Large-scale AI access has ten-working-day review after cutoff; Executive Director reviews and approves the selected list and may seek additional review.
facts.coordinateUse: Identifies an actual approval route for AI awards.
facts.limits: Does not confer authority for unrestricted external model inspection; models remain user-owned.

facts.claim: 273 of 299 benchmark proposals were awarded in 2025; development awarded 532 of 577.
facts.population: all EuroHPC systems, not only LUMI
facts.coordinateUse: Evidence the fast administrative channel operates at scale.
facts.limits: Never use 273/299 or 532/577 as probability of accepting new safeguard terms.

gaps.reason: Historical awards and AI-category composition found; no current signed safety appendix or consumed node-hour trace tied to it.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Recipient award ledger plus metered utilisation and versioned accepted terms.

gaps.reason: Access Policy locates award approval by mode, but award approval is not sufficient evidence of competence to change policy or third-party model-access rights.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Board decision approving policy amendment or explicit lawful delegated pilot authority; CSC and recipient agreement.

gaps.reason: Annual strategic table uses approximately eight GPU-hours per node-hour while Belgian instructions specify four package-hours.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Obtain each ledger's GPU/GCD definition and account only in reconciled units.

coordinateReadiness.x: Good process inputs: 2-week, 1-month, 10-working-day and 4-month paths plus actual award counts. New-condition adoption remains unknown.
coordinateReadiness.y: Historical AI-labelled awards and matched competitive node-hour denominator now available. Do not substitute them for prospective protected usage or causal safety effect.

facts.claim: All national channels together allocate half of LUMI resources.
facts.coordinateUse: Whole-coalition conditional envelope.
facts.limits: Do not add Belgian 7.4% to this 50%; neither is current protected usage.

facts.claim: Access documentation lists eleven national country channels with named operational allocators.
facts.locator: Resource Allocator table, excluding EuroHPC rows
facts.coordinateUse: Coordination scope, not legal-veto denominator.
facts.limits: Belgium lists two bodies; Denmark consortium universities; several bodies are consortia, not single legal signatories.

facts.claim: LUMI users had consumed 140 million GPU-hours by the June 2025 report.
facts.coordinateUse: System-scale context absent from earlier notes.
facts.limits: Not national-only, not period-matched annual denominator; do not multiply by quotas or AI share without harmonisation.

facts.claim: CSC reports more than half of LUMI computing resources used for AI-related research and innovation.
facts.unit: strict lower threshold of reported share
facts.coordinateUse: Shows AI use is material rather than assuming all compute is AI.
facts.limits: Measurement unit and channel breakdown absent; value denotes >0.5, not an exact estimate, and cannot be applied to each national quota.

facts.claim: CSC reported nearly 7,000 users across Europe.
facts.coordinateUse: Potential administrative scaling context.
facts.limits: Not recipient organisations, active users or independent agreement count.

facts.claim: January 2026 retrospective reports around 3,500 research projects since launch.
facts.coordinateUse: Inventory scale context.
facts.limits: Not number of models or national-channel awards; repeat project/user overlap unresolved.

facts.claim: Finnish development and benchmark projects each have maximum 5,000 GPU-hours; regular projects maximum 100,000.
facts.coordinateUse: Smaller national pilot scale; contrasts with Belgian cap.
facts.limits: Not awarded use; reconcile package/die accounting before cross-country arithmetic.

facts.claim: Finnish development and benchmark applications are reviewed in 1–4 weekdays by a Resource Officer.
facts.unit: weekdays upper end of published range
facts.coordinateUse: One national path can support a prompt small pilot.
facts.limits: No observed distribution; not coalition amendment time.

facts.claim: Finnish regular applications take 1–2 weeks and the Resource Allocation Board normally meets fortnightly.
facts.unit: weeks upper end of published range
facts.coordinateUse: Real approval body and cadence.
facts.limits: The 9 November 2026 application date is a compute deadline, not consent to shared evidence terms.

facts.claim: Next Finnish Extreme Scale call is announced for spring 2027.
facts.locator: Other LUMI resources: Finnish LUMI Extreme Scale Access
facts.coordinateUse: Newly located pre-Geneva opportunity.
facts.limits: No exact closing, award or completion date; cannot guarantee a full-year project completes by Geneva.

facts.claim: Czech national competition is announced three times yearly: February, June and October.
facts.coordinateUse: Asynchronous national coordination cadence.
facts.limits: Not confirmed 2027 exact dates; page excludes industrial users from this national offer.

facts.claim: Polish test grants accept continuous applications and last 30 days; regular grants last 12 months with two competitions yearly.
facts.coordinateUse: Short pilot precedent; monthly progress monitoring for regular grants.
facts.limits: No common coalition calendar or appendix adoption shown.

facts.claim: Eight Danish universities provide local Front Offices for HPC and data-management support.
facts.coordinateUse: Resolves why Denmark's single allocator label hides institutional complexity.
facts.limits: Not eight required vetoes or approvals for every Danish award.

facts.claim: A common six-month utilisation cut policy applies in national and EuroHPC non-industrial regular/extreme projects; allocation reduced to 60% unless usage exceeds 40%, with at least one month's notice.
facts.population: eligible projects in both LUMI pools
facts.coordinateUse: Concrete cross-channel implementation precedent.
facts.limits: Utilisation management, not a model-safety sanction; no evidence of legal equivalence for the proposed protocol.

gaps.reason: System aggregates, all country guides and several national rules found; no harmonised eleven-country AI award/usage ledger.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Join national award returns with LUMI project IDs and AI declaration fields; retain consumed versus allocated units and accounting definitions.

gaps.reason: Finnish board/officers, Swedish NAC, Dutch NWO/SURF and country allocators identified. Consortium policy signatories and amendment mandates not fully established.
gaps.nextRetrieval: National delegation decisions and consortium service-amendment governance; recipient evidence/data agreements for the selected pilot.

gaps.reason: No reviewed national guide or shared terms adopts the proposed evaluation-access/incident appendix. This does not prove universal absence.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Versioned accepted common schema, channel-specific adoption acts and measured pilot outcome; do not equate technical support contacts with consent.

coordinateReadiness.x: Several actual approval cadences and a shared operational rule now documented; coalition consent and full legal signatory set remain incomplete.
coordinateReadiness.y: 50% conditional envelope; material system AI use and national per-project ceilings. Country-specific actual AI usage and adopted coverage still missing.

facts.claim: Swissgrid reports 913 GWh positive control energy in 2025.
facts.locator: p.144 Key figures on grid-related energy transition, 2025 column
facts.coordinateUse: Historical scale of the process the Optimizer operates in; stronger than national electricity as a proxy.
facts.limits: Not all demonstrably controlled by the same model; no pilot-protected numerator; not AI-facility consumption.

facts.claim: Swissgrid reports 506 GWh negative control energy in 2025.
facts.coordinateUse: Separate direction of affected process; do not net away operational exposure.
facts.limits: Not actual safety effect or whole-grid coverage.

facts.claim: Secondary balancing-energy activations decreased 22% comparing the first ten months of 2025 with the same months of 2024; Swissgrid attributes this to multiple measures including forecasting and Optimizer Autopilot.
facts.coordinateUse: Evidence of operational integration and potential baseline covariates.
facts.limits: Not causal attribution to AI, fallback or the proposed safeguard; not reliability improvement measured by outages avoided.

facts.claim: The team moved the existing decision-support tool into productive automatic operation between January and May 2025.
facts.locator: The turning point in the project / Der Wendepunkt im Projekt
facts.coordinateUse: Demonstrates operator-owned implementation ability within months after earlier development.
facts.limits: Not total development duration, not a four-month estimated pilot SLA; preceding theses/prototypes took unspecified time.

facts.claim: The 2026 control-energy CSV contains 28,608 data rows plus a header, from 1 January 00:00 through 25 October 23:45.
facts.locator: semicolon CSV; line count minus header; Date Time first/last row
facts.coordinateUse: Concrete public input inventory for an offline replay feasibility study.
facts.limits: Rows include missing cells and local-time/DST ambiguity; not 28,608 independent fault episodes or model action logs.

facts.claim: Control-area-balance CSV contains 29,088 data rows with UTC timestamps from 31 December 2025 23:00 to 30 October 2026 22:45.
facts.locator: semicolon CSV; Date Time [UTC]; total rows minus header
facts.coordinateUse: Data includes system imbalance and covered aFRR/mFRR need; usable evidence availability input.
facts.limits: Aggregate operational states do not identify the Optimizer version, fallback trigger or recovery success.

facts.claim: Published CSV timestamps advance in quarter-hour intervals in inspected rows.
facts.locator: first seven and last three rows of each file
facts.coordinateUse: Resolution limit for externally reproducible work.
facts.limits: Cannot validate sub-second frequency control or fast fallback latency; full continuity/DST and missingness audit still required.

gaps.reason: Operator deployment account, annual process volumes and public time series found. None supplies matched AI-on/off fallback faults, controller action logs or recovery timing.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Operator-authorised simulator/action logs, version history, fallback success criteria and matched fault corpus; public aggregate CSV alone is insufficient.

gaps.reason: In-house teams and management involvement known; no pilot-specific delegation or model/replay licence found.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Swissgrid approved test charter and rights register, with any indispensable vendor permission.

gaps.reason: Public records concern balancing process, not electricity deliveries to a declared set of AI facilities. That earlier denominator is poorly matched to this operator-control route.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Prefer process-specific controlled dispatch volume after agreeing route scope; if AI-facility denominator is retained, obtain a facility-level metered population rather than national output.

coordinateReadiness.x: Public replay inputs and implementation precedent now concrete; model access, authorisation and test performance missing.
coordinateReadiness.y: 913/506 GWh process-volume context available. Pilot covers no established fraction of this process; causal safety reach remains unmeasured.

facts.claim: DESNZ call closes 6 November 2026, six calendar days after the observation date.
facts.coordinateUse: Immediate input deadline.
facts.limits: Submitting evidence is not operator authorisation or implemented safeguards.

facts.claim: Ofgem decided to establish a twelve-month AI technical sandbox pilot.
facts.coordinateUse: Relevant existing implementation vehicle, beyond DESNZ consultation alone.
facts.limits: Not a continuously open sandbox or a twelve-month award for our proposal; launch subject to readiness.

facts.claim: Ofgem received 32 consultation responses.
facts.coordinateUse: Evidence of programme-level engagement.
facts.limits: Not 32 consents to this safeguard, trial participants or independent required approvals.

facts.claim: Applications targeted late autumn 2026 and initial testing rounds from early 2027; published lessons targeted end-2027.
facts.coordinateUse: Some testing may fit before Geneva but final programme evaluation is later.
facts.limits: No exact dates or selected cohorts; no evidence our route is accepted.

facts.claim: Lead applicants must be licensees, market participants or essential-service operators; technology partners work under lead accountability; testing is separated from live systems.
facts.coordinateUse: Concrete owner and permissions path for a bounded trial.
facts.limits: Participation gives neither regulatory approval nor deployment endorsement; governance details await participation guidance.

facts.claim: DESNZ reports NESO balancing instructions rose tenfold between December 2023 and June 2025 to over 200,000.
facts.population: NESO balancing-control instructions, period basis as reported
facts.locator: A more distributed, dynamic and digital system; footnote 5
facts.coordinateUse: Operational complexity context and candidate workload, not generic national MW.
facts.limits: Underlying NESO page returned 403; exact count period not independently verified. Not AI-only or the selected pilot population.

facts.claim: DESNZ identifies NESO's Volta programme as an AI forecasting/optimisation/control-room workstream and links its primary account.
facts.coordinateUse: Specific future retrieval/owner target rather than unspecified UK operator.
facts.limits: NESO original returned 403; not acceptance, procurement terms or known affected assets.

gaps.reason: Regulator sandbox, lead eligibility and NESO programme identified, but no selected operator for our route, asset roster or covered MW/MWh.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Autumn participation guidance and selected use-case agreements; operator workflow inventory and replay data.

gaps.reason: Both primary NESO Volta and skip-rate pages returned 403 through direct fetch; government citations and sandbox decision provide partial alternatives, not originals.
gaps.nextRetrieval: NESO data portal/download mirrors and published control-room performance packs with exact instruction-period definitions.

gaps.reason: Evidence call and regulator pilot decision specify testability and governance but no per-use-case response-time, cost, veto count or accepted fallback success threshold.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Selected pilot technical charter, contract/data rights and budget; measured baseline and fault results.

coordinateReadiness.x: Substantially improved: an existing regulator-authorised sandbox design and early-2027 testing target, but no route acceptance or fixed completion date.
coordinateReadiness.y: Candidate control-room decision volumes only. No pilot-specific affected resource denominator or demonstrated risk-reduction coefficient.

facts.claim: ICO evidence call closes at the end of 20 November 2026, twenty days after observation.
facts.locator: Closing date and How to respond
facts.coordinateUse: Immediate path to provide test design/evidence.
facts.limits: No commitment to incorporate submitted recommendations.

facts.claim: ICO roadmap targets agentic guidance publication in spring 2027.
facts.coordinateUse: Potential pre-Geneva regulatory output.
facts.limits: Roadmap still labels consultation forthcoming though live call is open; target is not a delivery guarantee.

facts.claim: ICO selected eleven priority foundation-model developers for supervision.
facts.population: Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Cohere, DeepSeek, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Stability AI, X.AI
facts.coordinateUse: Concrete evidence the institution reaches significant model providers.
facts.limits: Not agent deployment census, affected market share or participating pilot counterparties.

facts.claim: Ten developers made or committed to changes following supervision; X.AI's engagement was suspended during formal investigation.
facts.locator: News, Industry improvements; report, opening and named actions
facts.coordinateUse: Precedent of influence, not exact-safeguard consent.
facts.limits: Do not treat 10/11 as completion or cooperation probability; interventions and commitments differ.

facts.claim: Report explicitly names Apple, Cohere and OpenAI as having made transparency-information changes.
facts.locator: Transparency and information rights, first paragraph
facts.coordinateUse: Separates demonstrably described completed actions from promises.
facts.limits: Not exhaustive completed-change count, no independent audit, and not agent permissions/fallback changes.

facts.claim: ICO reports enquiries to OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and UK AISI about recent agent testing/deployment.
facts.coordinateUse: Agent-specific supervisory activity and possible evidence sources.
facts.limits: Three developers plus one institute, not four deployers; no findings or adjudicated failure count.

facts.claim: ICO's sandbox had helped more than 25 organisations by its fifth anniversary.
facts.locator: Tackling complexity and burden, Regulatory Sandbox paragraph
facts.coordinateUse: Institutional capacity precedent for collaborative evidence work.
facts.limits: Not agentic-AI pilot count, acceptance rate, completion duration or available slots.

facts.claim: Sixteen organisations likely to use automated decision-making about jobseekers committed to act on ICO recommendations.
facts.coordinateUse: Adjacent implementation channel with explicit commitment count.
facts.limits: Not completed changes, not general agent deployment reach, not consent to this protocol.

gaps.reason: Call, supervised developer inventory and annual innovation outputs do not disclose a frozen population of agent workflows/executions affected by this proposal.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Select a deployer; obtain versioned workflow inventory, execution counts and tool-permission baseline.

gaps.reason: Completed transparency actions and mixed commitments found; no matched agent-permission/logging test outcomes or causal incident reduction.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Public pilot results with allowed/unauthorised denominators, false refusals and independently scored accountability reconstruction.

gaps.reason: Regulator activity and target are clear; no proposed-safeguard incorporation decision or named deployer acceptance found.
gaps.nextRetrieval: Current Information Commission delegation/approval record and signed deployer pilot terms; provider permission only if required by chosen interface.

coordinateReadiness.x: Defined evidence window, spring guidance target and institutional precedents; adoption/completion probabilities remain unidentified.
coordinateReadiness.y: Eleven-priority-developer inventory demonstrates institutional reach, not route coverage. Workflow execution population and effect sizes missing.
